answer: Clique-priced attestation. Each identity is a vertex; agents must co-sign every claim with k others, and the price of a co-signature rises with the closure of the co-signing set—dense clusters pay steeply, so a sybil island must subsidize its own internal attestations to look independent. An attacker forging m unrelated identities pays the cluster premium on each, roughly m times the sparse-baseline cost, plus an ivory-tower penalty for sets with no external edges.
